answers.name: Gala
answers.fact: A New Zealand seedling from the 1930s, now the most-grown apple in the US.

answers.name: Red Delicious
answers.fact: Bred for looks and shipping durability more than flavour.

answers.name: Granny Smith
answers.fact: A chance seedling found in an Australian compost heap in the 1860s.

answers.name: Fuji
answers.fact: Developed in Japan, named for the town of Fujisaki rather than the mountain.

answers.name: Honeycrisp
answers.fact: Bred in Minnesota for cells that rupture loudly when bitten.

answers.name: Golden Delicious
answers.fact: Unrelated to Red Delicious; a parent of both Gala and Jonagold.

answers.name: McIntosh
answers.fact: Found in Ontario in 1811. The computer was named after it, spelling changed.

answers.name: Cripps Pink
answers.fact: Sold under the Pink Lady trademark, which is a brand rather than a variety name.

answers.name: Braeburn
answers.fact: Another New Zealand chance seedling; keeps for months in storage.

answers.name: Jonagold
answers.fact: A Jonathan and Golden Delicious cross out of Cornell.

answers.name: Cosmic Crisp
answers.fact: Released in 2019 after two decades of breeding at Washington State.

answers.name: Cortland
answers.fact: Slow to brown when cut, which made it a salad standard.

answers.name: Arkansas Black
answers.fact: Nearly purple-black, and almost inedible until it has sat for two months.

answers.name: Newtown Pippin
answers.fact: Franklin sent them to London. America's first commercially exported apple.

answers.name: Esopus Spitzenburg
answers.fact: Said to have been Thomas Jefferson's favourite.
